chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is given to the Zakat collector?' He said, 'Whatever the Imam sees (appropriate), and nothing is fixed/measured out for him.'

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam (specifically the Imam of the time in Shia context)
key_terms.يُقَدَّرُ: Fixed or measured out (as a specific amount)

ai.seo_question: What is the fixed salary of the Zakat collector in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the compensation for the Mushaddiq is discretionary (mufrada) rather than fixed, reflecting the Imam's authority to determine fair remuneration based on the collector's effort and the treasury's capacity. In Shia jurisprudence, this flexibility distinguishes the role from fixed salaries, emphasizing the Imam's judicial discretion in administrative matters. The ruling underscores the practical administration of Zakat funds under the guidance of the Imam.
